basic_details.offering_entity: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST, Daegu, South Korea / Ministry of Science and ICT)
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: DGIST Main Campus (Dalseong-gun, Daegu, South Korea)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Open to all graduate departments: Emerging Materials Science, Information and Communication Engineering (Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Cybersecurity, IoT), Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering, Energy Science & Engineering, Brain and Cognitive Sciences, and New Biology.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~100% of admitted international graduate students receive full fellowship support (~80 to 100 new graduate students admitted annually)
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open international competition; Pakistani graduates in computing, robotics, and materials have strong representation (typically 5 to 10 awardees/yr)
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: Up to 2 years for MS; up to 4 years for PhD; up to 5 years for Integrated MS-PhD, contingent upon satisfactory academic progress

nationality_requirements: Open to international applicants holding non-Korean citizenship
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Completed 4-year Bachelor's degree (16 years education) for MS; completed Master's degree (18 years education) for PhD in science or engineering with minimum 3.20 / 4.00 CGPA (3.50+ competitive from recognized Pakistani universities like NUST, FAST-NUCES, GIKI, UET, LUMS, PIEAS).
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Equivalence to 80%+ marks or 3.20/4.00 CGPA; evaluated on cumulative transcript.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Substantial undergraduate coursework in computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, materials, or biosciences.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated or currently in final semester of degree graduating before semester start.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Laboratory research experience, peer-reviewed publications, and coding competition achievements provide a competitive advantage.

english_proficiency.notes: TOEFL iBT min 80, IELTS Academic min 6.5, or official English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate from an accredited Pakistani university.

eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Korean language not required; all graduate courses, seminars, and lab meetings are conducted in English.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Elite graduate researchers in robotics, AI, brain science, and emerging materials.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot hold another full national Korean government scholarship concurrently.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition waiver provided for all semesters of normal degree duration (KRW 3,500,000/semester waived completely).

admission_application_fee.details: DGIST charges no application fee for international graduate applicants.

accommodation.details: On-campus modern graduate dormitories provided (double room ~KRW 150,000 to 200,000/month; single room ~KRW 250,000/month), paid from stipend.

monthly_stipend.details: Monthly student stipend: Master's students receive KRW 750,000 to 1,000,000/month (~PKR 155,000 to 205,000/mo); PhD students receive KRW 1,150,000 to 1,500,000/month (~PKR 235,000 to 310,000/mo) via university fellowship and research assistantships.

airfare.details: Initial airfare to South Korea is self-funded.

visa_fee.details: South Korean D-2 student visa application fee ($60) paid to Korean Embassy in Islamabad.

health_insurance.details: Korean National Health Insurance (NHIS) monthly premiums (~KRW 75,000/month) are subsidized or supported by departmental research funds.

food_allowance.details: Living expenses covered by monthly stipend; subsidized campus cafeterias provide meals at KRW 4,000 - 5,500/meal.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: High-tech laboratories provide advanced research equipment, supercomputing resources, and materials.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Professors fully fund international conference travel, registration, and lodging for students with accepted papers.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Free campus shuttle buses connect DGIST campus to Daegok subway station in downtown Daegu.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single institution (DGIST, Daegu, South Korea - Specialized National Research Institute alongside KAIST, UNIST, GIST)
participating_institutions: DGIST (Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology, Dalseong Campus)
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: One of South Korea's four prestigious national science and technology institutes (KAIST, GIST, DGIST, UNIST); QS World Top 50 in Citations per Faculty.
available_majors: Information and Communication Engineering (Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Cybersecurity)
Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering (Medical Robotics, Autonomous Systems)
Energy Science and Engineering (Secondary Batteries, Solar Cells, Hydrogen)
Brain and Cognitive Sciences (Neurodegenerative Diseases, Neural Engineering)
New Biology (Synthetic Biology, Aging and Regeneration)
university_and_program_options.program_duration: Master's: 2 years; PhD: 4 years; Integrated MS-PhD: 5 years.
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor's/Master's degree with minimum 3.2+ CGPA, online application, research statement, 2 recommendation letters, and English proficiency certificate (IELTS, TOEFL, or MOI).
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Information & Communication Engineering (AI) and Robotics have high applicant volume; Emerging Materials and Energy Science have exceptional lab funding and high admission yields.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Contacting a prospective DGIST lab professor prior to applying is strongly encouraged. Review the lab publications, send your CV and research interests, and obtain an agreement of prospective supervision to maximize scholarship and admission success.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the DGIST online admissions portal during the open application window, fill in personal/academic details, and upload required documents.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Explore research laboratories on the DGIST department website and contact potential professors.
Step 2: Access the DGIST online application portal during the application period (Spring: Sept/Oct; Fall: March/April).
Step 3: Complete the online application form and select your department and degree level.
Step 4: Upload scanned academic transcripts, degree certificates, and English test certificate/MOI.
Step 5: Upload your Statement of Purpose (SOP) and Study Plan.
Step 6: Register contact details for two academic referees who will submit recommendation letters.
Step 7: Submit the application (no application fee required).
Step 8: Document screening results announced within 3-4 weeks.
Step 9: Shortlisted candidates attend an online video interview (15-20 minutes via Zoom) with faculty.
Step 10: Final admission and scholarship decisions announced; accept offer, receive Certificate of Admission (CoA), and apply for Korean D-2 visa.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: 100% integrated: admission to DGIST automatically carries the full tuition waiver and monthly fellowship package.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Two recommendation letters submitted online by referees via the DGIST referee portal.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of Purpose: Describe your academic background, scientific motivation, research goals, and why DGIST is your chosen institution.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Detailed study plan outlining proposed research topics, methodologies, and timeline during graduate study.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV detailing education, laboratory techniques, programming languages, publications, and awards.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical/research interview (15-20 minutes via Zoom) conducted in English by a 3-member faculty panel evaluating technical background and research motivation.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: TOEFL iBT (80+), IELTS Academic (6.5+), or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate. GRE not required.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Color scanned copies uploaded at application; verified original degree certificates (apostilled or consular legalized) submitted upon arrival.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English translations for all non-English documents.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Clear color copy of passport identification page.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Ensure name spelling matches educational documents.

required_documents_checklist.document_name: Official Academic Transcripts and Degree Certificate
required_documents_checklist.specification: Complete transcripts of Bachelor's and Master's degrees showing all semester courses, credits, and grades.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan attested documents.

required_documents_checklist.document_name: Statement of Purpose (SOP) and Study Plan
required_documents_checklist.specification: 1 to 2 page essay outlining technical background, research goals, and alignment with DGIST faculty.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Highlight specific DGIST research labs and proposed research topics.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Academic CV detailing publications, research projects, technical skills, and honors.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Highlight laboratory equipment experience and software/programming capabilities.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Confidential letters from university professors or research mentors.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Referees should submit from official institutional email addresses.

required_documents_checklist.document_name: English Language Proficiency Certificate or MOI
required_documents_checklist.specification: Official IELTS (6.5+), TOEFL (80+), or official university Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Official MOI certificate from Pakistani university registrar is accepted.

important_dates_timeline.application_open_date: Spring Intake: Early September; Fall Intake: Early March
important_dates_timeline.application_deadline: Spring Intake: Late October; Fall Intake: Late April
important_dates_timeline.visa_application_window: January (Spring) / July (Fall) (Korean D-2 visa processing via Korean Embassy Islamabad)
important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Two full intake cycles per year (Spring semester starts in March; Fall semester starts in September).

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 35% (Undergraduate/Master's GPA and coursework rigor in core engineering/science subjects)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 30% (Prior laboratory experience, thesis quality, publications, and technical skills)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 10% (Clarity, depth, and feasibility of Statement of Purpose and Study Plan)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: DGIST Departmental Admissions Committee comprising senior faculty members.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Two-phase review: Initial document screening evaluates GPA, curriculum match, and research background. Shortlisted candidates undergo a 15-20 minute online video interview with a 3-member faculty panel evaluating technical depth and research passion. Admitted students receive full fellowship support.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~800 to 1,200 international applicants apply across both intake cycles
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~80 to 100 fully funded graduate fellowships awarded annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~10% (Strong success rate for graduates from NUST, FAST, GIKI, UET with good research backgrounds)
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: 3.50+ / 4.00 CGPA (78%+ aggregate with strong lab experience)
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Graduates in engineering or science with solid laboratory experience, good programming skills, and clear research direction.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates in Information & Communication Engineering, Robotics, Materials Science, Energy Engineering, and Biosciences.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, India, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Uzbekistan, Iran.

fake_websites_and_scams: Unauthorized consultancies charging placement fees for DGIST scholarships. DGIST charges ZERO application fee and awards fellowships directly.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: DGIST application is 100% free. Never pay application processing fees to third parties.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Do not hire agents. Communicating directly with prospective professors demonstrates research independence.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Flight tickets between Pakistan and Daegu / Seoul Incheon (~PKR 150,000 - 220,000).
Medical check-up and tuberculosis test required for Korean visa and dormitory entry (~PKR 15,000 - 25,000).
Initial living expenses before first monthly stipend disbursement (~KRW 300,000 - 500,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: CLAIM: Korean language proficiency is required. (FACT: DGIST is 100% English-medium for all graduate programs).
CLAIM: GRE scores are required. (FACT: DGIST does NOT require GRE scores).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Some commercial blogs state DGIST covers round-trip international airfare; official DGIST regulations confirm initial flights are self-funded.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 / 4.30 in all graduate coursework to retain scholarship funding.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical research and laboratory participation on the DGIST campus in Daegu.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Annual research progress evaluations conducted by the thesis advisory committee.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: International students holding a D-2 visa may work up to 20 hours/week with university and immigration permission, but graduate assistantship duties require full-time commitment.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None. International graduates from Korean STEM institutions are eligible for the D-10 job seeker visa and pathways to F-2-7 points-based residency.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: None; scholars fulfill standard graduate research assistantship duties in their assigned laboratory.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Funding terminates upon withdrawal; no clawback of past disbursed stipend or waived tuition.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Requires approval from both department chairs and the Dean of Graduate School.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Scholarship is granted for the nominal duration of the program; extensions require supervisor grant funding.

data_points_missing_or_unpublished_by_so: Departmental laboratory research grant budget ceilings across individual labs.
Exact quota allocation between MS, PhD, and Integrated MS-PhD programs.
